subject: Commercial qualification: cost targets & host price comparison
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@optimahealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@optimahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial qualification: cost targets & host price comparison
Attachments: pricing-sweep-20270412.csv

Hi Michael / Priya —

Great to chat earlier. Quick recap and the items we agreed to follow up on related to cost/price targets so your procurement and finance teams can evaluate: 

Call highlights / context
- Expected monthly volume: 30M – 80M input+output tokens (peaks up to ~150M in promotional months).
- Primary workload: real-time chat + short-document summarization (median response length ~120 tokens).
- Latency requirement: p95 <= 350ms for chat flows in US regions.
- Data needs: no long-term retention; customer-controlled KMS preferred.

Budget / target unit economics (from your side)
- Target unit price: $/1M tokens in the $300–$600 range (you mentioned $500 as an internal target).
- Annualized budget window: $200k – $850k depending on final unit price and usage growth.

What I attached / benchmarking we ran
- Attached CSV: pricing-sweep-20270412.csv with a simple per-token cost model and three candidate Redwood offers (standard, committed, and committed+quantization).
- Also included a short Redwood benchmarking PDF that compares host-level $/1M token equivalents for common providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, two leading open-model hosts) under three run profiles (low-latency chat, batch embed, high-throughput rerank).

Preliminary takeaways (high level)
- To hit $500 / 1M tokens at your volume, the committed tier + 8-bit quantized runtime gets us closest in unit costs while preserving p95 latency targets for chat.
- OpenAI/Anthropic list prices translate to roughly $420–$1,100 / 1M depending on model and batching assumptions; open-hosts (self-hosted managed partners) can be lower but vary greatly by SLA and region.

Requested next steps
1) Please confirm the expected steady-state monthly volume (pick a single working number: 30M, 50M, or 80M).
2) Can you share whether procurement needs a formal one-pager comparing list vs committed offers? (We can provide a short TCO summary + assumptions.)
3) Proposed next meeting: 30–45 minute pricing + SLA alignment with finance & infra (Marissa + Rafael to join). Options: Wed Apr 14 10:00 AM PT or Thu Apr 15 9:00 AM PT.

Thanks — I’ll prep the baseline TCO table and host benchmark so we can move quickly.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0184

Thanks Jasmine — helpful summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) Volume: steady-state expectation is closer to the 50M tokens/month bucket. We may ramp to ~100–120M/month in Q4 if the pilot shows product-market fit.
2) Target price: finance flagged $500/1M as the threshold they'd be comfortable with given our current ARR targets. If committed pricing can get close to that with SLA, that's attractive.
3) Benchmark asks: Finance explicitly wants a side-by-side of Redwood committed offer vs the following: OpenAI gpt-4o (or comparable), Anthropic Claude Pro, and "OpenHostX" (their managed open-model host). Include assumed sequence lengths, batching, and any discounts baked into the $/1M conversion.

Latency question: your p95 number — is that measured on Redwood Hosted? We need clarity on whether committed/dedicated deployments (with private VPC) maintain the same latency profile. Also, please call out any additional fees (eg. multi-region replication, KMS).

We can do the pricing + SLA alignment Wed Apr 14 at 10:00 AM PT. Please send a calendar invite with dial-in and the short TCO doc.

-Michael

Marissa / Rafael — internal update before the 4/14 call with OptimaHealth.

Summary of external asks (from Michael):
- Confirm steady-state at ~50M tokens/month with Q4 ramp to 100–120M.
- Finance wants side-by-side committed vs OpenAI/Anthropic/OpenHostX with conversion assumptions.
- Need explicit SLA/latency mapping for Hosted vs Dedicated/Private deployments and any mgmt fees for KMS/multi-region.

My proposal for what we bring to the 4/14 meeting:
1) One-page TCO (attached) with three Redwood offers:
   - Offer A: Hosted — pay-as-you-go (no commit). Baseline list $/1M for standard float model.
   - Offer B: Committed 6/12-month — volume discounts to hit $/1M in the $450–$650 band depending on quantization and KV cache assumptions.
   - Offer C: Dedicated reserved capacity — lowest unit price when 12-month commit + quantization enabled; includes optional multi-region replication (extra fee).
2) Benchmark appendix (separate PDF): modeled $/1M equivalents for OpenAI, Anthropic, and two partner-managed open hosts using our standard assumptions (median seq 120 tokens, batching 6 for chat, 1.5x overhead for system tokens).
3) SLA slip-ups to call out: committed offers require 30-day lead for capacity increases; dedicated has stronger latency guarantees and private VPC (but higher base fee).

Numbers I'm planning to present (ballpark for discussion) — all $/1M tokens equivalent:
- Redwood Hosted (paygo): $1,000 – $1,700 (depends on model).
- Redwood Committed (50M/month): $480 – $620 (with quantized variant nearing $420 at 12mo commit + burst profile).
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved): $350 – $480 (best-case at sustained 80M+).
- OpenAI (published list -> our equivalents): $420 – $900 depending on model + prompt length.
- Anthropic: $480 – $1,100 depending on model and batch.
- OpenHostX (managed): $320 – $560 (varies; often lower but with SLA caveats).

Questions for you both:
- Accept these ballpark numbers to take into the external call, or do you want tighter modeling before Wed? I can tighten the CSV to show the assumptions if you want to share exact sequencing and batching they expect.
- Rafael — can you confirm whether we should include a short note about KMS/HSM fees and a line item for multi-region replication?

I attached the pricing sweep CSV and the benchmark PDF for your review. If these look good I’ll convert Offer B into a preliminary term sheet to show finance on the call.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
